children: WASHOUT HOLDS, REBOUND EMERGES

A strong rebound is taking shape ahead of Friday's open as investors return from the Thanksgiving break and pile back into beaten-down AI and technology shares. US stock futures are sharply higher, with E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures up more than 2%, easily leading the advance.
From a technical perspective, Wednesday may have been more important than it first appeared. Both E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures
and E-mini S&P 500 futures
carved out bullish hammer candlesticks, a pattern that often emerges near market lows when buyers step in and reverse an earlier selloff.
The signal was especially notable because it developed as the major indexes, including the Nasdaq 100
, held above last week's panic lows. In other words, sellers failed to gain fresh downside traction, leaving the door open for a rebound.
That follow-through is emerging Friday morning. Nearly every S&P Select Sector SPDR fund is trading higher ahead of the bell, with 7 of the 11 sectors up more than 1%. Technology
is the clear leader, gaining more than 2.5%, while consumer staples
is the lone sector modestly in the red.
Elsewhere, regional banks
are up about 0.8%, while chip stocks are among the market's standout performers. The PHLX Semiconductor ETF
is jumping more than 4% as investors return to growth-oriented areas of the market.
Retailers are also getting a lift from holiday shopping expectations. Adobe forecasts a record $12.9 billion in online Black Friday spending this year, up 9.2% from a year ago. The S&P Retail ETF
is up about 0.8% in premarket trading.

Investors should keep in mind that Friday's session is shortened, with US stock markets closing at 1 p.m. ET and bond markets at 2 p.m. ET. Historically, the post-Thanksgiving trading day is one of the lightest-volume sessions of the year, which can sometimes amplify market moves.
Here is a snapshot of where markets stood around 8:55 a.m. ET.
US equity index futures rally: Nasdaq 100 up >2%
STOXX 600 index gains ~1%
Dollar gains; bitcoin, US crude both up ~1%; gold up >2%
US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~4.90%
